question: What is the primary purpose of microbial taxonomy in healthcare?

options.A: To determine the exact cost of laboratory tests
options.B: To destroy harmful pathogens on hospital surfaces
options.C: To organize and identify microorganisms systematically
options.D: To calculate the growth rate of human cells

explanation: Taxonomy gives healthcare workers a standardized system to classify and name microorganisms for clear communication. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which part of the scientific name *Staphylococcus aureus* represents the genus?
explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first capitalized word always designates the genus, while the second indicates the species. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the highest and broadest rank in biological classification?
explanation: The domain sits at the very top of the taxonomic hierarchy, dividing life into major cellular categories. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h2)

question: The suffix *-aceae* at the end of a microbial name typically indicates which taxonomic rank?
explanation: Microbiological nomenclature conventionally assigns the suffix *-aceae* to identify the family rank. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h2)

question: What color do Gram-negative bacteria appear after the complete Gram staining procedure?
explanation: Gram-negative cells lose the crystal violet stain during decolorization and take up the pink safranin counterstain. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h3)

question: A laboratory report describes spherical bacteria clustered together like grapes. What term describes this arrangement?
explanation: The prefix staphylo- indicates clusters, and cocci refers to spherical shapes, typical of organisms like *Staphylococcus aureus*. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h3)

question: What protective protein coat surrounds the viral genetic material?
explanation: The capsid is the protein shell that encases and protects the viral nucleic acid genome. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient is diagnosed with an infection caused by a virus possessing an outer lipid bilayer. What is this outer layer called?
explanation: Many animal viruses acquire an outer membrane known as a viral envelope derived from host cell membranes during release. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which key cellular feature distinguishes fungi and parasites from bacteria?
explanation: Fungi and parasites are eukaryotic organisms characterized by true membrane-bound nuclei and organelles. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h5)

question: What type of organism is *Plasmodium*, the causative agent of malaria?
explanation: *Plasmodium* belongs to the protozoa group, which are single-celled eukaryotic parasites. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of molecular methods over traditional microbial staining?

options.A: Higher accuracy based on genetic blueprints
options.B: Elimination of the need for any laboratory equipment
options.C: Lower cost for every routine test
options.D: Ability to grow viruses on plain nutrient agar

explanation: Molecular methods analyze DNA and RNA, revealing true genetic relationships that visual appearance alone might hide. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which laboratory technology identifies microbes by analyzing their unique protein mass fingerprints?
explanation: MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry rapidly identifies microorganisms by matching their unique cellular protein profiles against a reference database. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h6)

question: A laboratory report identifies a patient's wound infection as a Gram-negative bacillus. How does this information assist nursing care?

options.A: It proves the patient has a viral respiratory illness
options.B: It shows that the infection will resolve without medical intervention
options.C: It indicates that no isolation precautions are ever required
options.D: It guides appropriate infection control and targeted antibiotic therapy

explanation: Knowing the specific bacterial classification helps the healthcare team select effective medications and implement proper barrier nursing. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why must nurses understand basic microbial classification during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To manufacture vaccines directly at the bedside
options.B: To apply correct isolation and barrier precautions effectively
options.C: To perform advanced gene sequencing in hospital rooms

explanation: Understanding how pathogens are categorized helps nurses anticipate transmission routes and apply appropriate containment measures. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h7)
